questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Bergen mostly because of the nature - I needed a change of scenery and to get some fresh air. I wanted to experience an everyday life where hikes and mountains could be easily integrated in my life as a student. It was also a high priority for me that the destination was reachable by train or another sustainable means of tranport.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy as I remember. All the information was to be found on UIB's website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive much assistance but it was easy to seek help on campus or on email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found my housing off campus after I arrived in Bergen. I startede by living in a student housing, but that wasn't for me. It was pretty easy to find another place to live for me but I think that was due to me already living in Bergen, so I could easily get in touch with the renters and go to see the rooms.
There is a lot of places on
finn.no

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's more expensive but a great way to get to know the city better and maybe live with some actual Norwegians. The students housing is mostly exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I actually can't really remember it.. I remember there being a lot of deadlines and a lot of different informations to fill out on different platforms but it wasn't too difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of emails that described what I needed to do and I could also get help by writing to them with questions - which I did.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very succesful! I got both of the classes that I wished for. First of the classes was filled when I went to register, but a couple of weeks before the semester start and went to check again and then the course was open for registration so I changed over to that one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just write them if you have any questions! It's easier than trying to figure it all out by yourself because it can be a quite overwhelming system.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There wasn't many options for students of anthropology at the University of Bergen. 
And the planning and schedules of the courses didn't really make sense to me. One course was only once a week and the other one didn't start until the end of October - which made the last couple of months really stressfull because the we had to learn an entire semster's syllabus in two months.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: One course was on BA-level and my other course could be taken as both BA and MA student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style compared fine with UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SANT105 - Power; it's articulations and disguises 
MVK210 - Music, gender and sexuality

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes! Go up a mountain, visit a gallery, go to a concert.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Meet them at a student bar and ask them out on a hike

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Their drinking culture is a bit different than what I'm used to. It's quite heavy and based alot around clubbing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It's a lot like here in Denmark

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Have patience with Norwegians - they are sweet but it takes time to get to know them. 
Enjoy the nature! 
Take advantage of all the things happening in the city. There is always an exhibition, a concert, a gallery opening or something else. It's an extremely cultural city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just say yes and get out of your comfort zone. There are so many things to do - try them out.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet new people and create a life for myself in a completely new city that was exciting and fulfilling.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To get to know Norwegians

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
